title: Heirloom Tomato & Ricotta Tart
featured_image_alt: Heirloom Tomato Tart
content:
Mother’s Day is just around the corner and this is the perfect easy tart to impress mum. Try this colourful and delicious Tomato & Ricotta Tart recipe from Tara Maini https://www.instagram.com/choperella/ 

It’s colourful and delicious! Just listen to the crunch! The perfect tart to celebrate with quality ingredients. 

 

Ingredients:

4-5 small heirloom tomatoes (such as Kumato, pineapple, chocolate, oxheart) 

200g ricotta

2 eggs

2 cloves garlic, minced

60g grated pecorino romano

1 sheet spelt wholemeal butter puff pastry (Regular puff pastry works too)

2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil

½ lemon juice and zest

15g fresh basil 

125g Wild rocket

Salt and pepper 

Flakey sea salt for garnish

 

Method:

  1. Preheat oven to 200°F. Line a baking tray with parchment paper, and set it aside. 

  2. Line another large baking sheet with paper towels. Slice the tomatoes crosswise ¼-inch thick. Set the sliced tomatoes on the paper towel in a single layer. 

  3. Season the tomatoes evenly with salt and pepper on both sides, cover with another paper towel, and sit for 15 minutes, allowing the salt to draw moisture out of the tomatoes.

  4. Mix the ricotta,1 egg, minced garlic, pecorino romano, ¼ teaspoon salt and pepper.

  5. Roll out the thawed pastry on the parchment-lined tray. Cut the pastry into a rough 35cm disc. Using a fork, prick the center of the pastry with minor marks to keep the pastry from puffing up in the centre during baking, 

  6. Spread the ricotta mixture over the centre of the pastry, leaving a 3cm border.

  7. Lay the tomato slices over the ricotta overlapping slightly, so that the tomatoes cover the ricotta. 

  8. Fold the pastry edge over the filling, pleating as you go, don’t worry if it’s not perfect, this is a rustic tart!

  9. Whisk the remaining 1 egg with 1 tsp water in a small bowl. Brush the pastry border with the egg wash. 

  10. Bake for 30-35 mins or until puffed golden brown on the edges.

  11. While the tart is baking make the side salad. Whisk together, extra virgin olive oil, lemon juice, zest, and a pinch of salt and pepper. 

  12. Tear ¾ of the basil leaves into a bowl along with the wild rocket. Drizzle over the dressing and toss to combine. 

  13. Garnish the ricotta tart with the remaining basil leaves. Season with flakey sea salt and freshly cracked pepper, as desired. Serve with the salad, enjoy!

title: Cheeseburger with Potato Wedges
content:
Cheeseburger with potato wedges and cabbage-carrot slaw recipe from @platedbyames

(serves two)

 

Ingredients: 

  • Burger patties
  • Brioche buns
  • Mixed greens
  • Red onion
  • Tomato
  • Pickles

Potato Wedges:

  • Red potatoes, washed
  • Salt
  • Olive oil
  • Minced garlic
  • Black pepper
  • Herb seasoning

Cabbage-Carrot Slaw:

  • Carrot
  • Red cabbage
  • Green cabbage
  • Apple cider vinegar
  • White wine vinegar
  • Honey
  • Olive oil
  • Salt

1. Start by cutting the washed red potatoes into wedges.

2. Season with salt and air fry at 180 C for 10 minutes.

3. Meanwhile, in a small bowl, combine the olive oil, minced garlic, black pepper, and herb seasoning. Mix well. 

4. After 10 minutes, transfer the wedges to a bowl and toss together with the mixture until all the wedges are evenly coated. 

5. Air fry for an additional 12-15 minutes until golden around the edges, shaking the basket halfway through.

6. Next, prepare the cabbage-carrot slaw. Julienne the carrot using a peeler, and shred both the red and green cabbages. Add them to a large bowl.

7. In a small bowl, whisk together the apple cider vinegar, white wine vinegar, honey, olive oil and salt. Pour over the cabbage and carrot mixture. 

8. Toss well to combine, then set aside. 

9. Time to make the burger! Season both sides of the patties with salt and pepper first. Then, prepare the sauce by whisking together the ketchup, mayo, and mustard. 

10. Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Once the pan is hot, add the patties to the pan and cook for 4-5 minutes (until a crust forms on the bottom of the patty). 

11. Flip the patties and cook for 2-3 more minutes. Add the cheese slices on top, cover the pan with a lid, and cook on lower heat for an additional 1-2 minutes. Remove the pan from heat and allow the patties to rest for around 4-5 minutes.

12. Assemble the brioche buns with mixed greens, burger patties, cheese, red onion, tomato, pickles, and sauce. 

13. Serve with the potato wedges and cabbage-carrot slaw. Enjoy!

title: Marry Me Chicken Pasta with Spinach
content:
Marry Me Chicken Pasta with Spinach

by Karlie Verkerk

Cook time 30 minutes

Serves 4

 

INGREDIENTS

400g Rummo mafaldine pasta

500g chicken breast

1 tsp garlic powder

1 tsp sweet paprika

2 tbsp olive oil

3 garlic cloves, minced

1 small brown onion, finely chopped

1 tsp dried oregano

1 tbsp tomato paste

1 jar Mutti pesto rosso

1 cup milk

2 large handfuls baby spinach

¼ cup finely grated Parmesan, plus extra to serve

 

METHOD

  1. Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil; cook pasta until al dente, reserve 2 cups of pasta cooking water.
  2. Dice chicken into 5cm cubes then add to a bowl with garlic powder and paprika; mix to combine.
  3. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a heavy-based saucepan or deep-sided frying pan over medium heat. Add chicken and cook until lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
  4. Add remaining olive oil, garlic, onion and oregano; cook for 2 minutes until onion is translucent. Turn heat down to low, add tomato paste and cook for a further 1 minute.
  5. Add jar of Rummo pesto and stir to combine. Then add milk, baby spinach, parmesan and cooked chicken; stir to combine and season with salt and pepper to taste.
  6. Once pasta is cooked, add to sauce along with some reserved pasta cooking water to help coat the pasta. Serve with extra grated parmesan on top.

title: Umami Sauce Beef Bowl
featured_image_alt: Hand Holding Beef Bowl
content:
Beef bowl or ‘Gyudon’ is a rice bowl topped with beef and onions. It’s one of the most popular fast foods in Japan and making Gyudon is really easy so please try it!

About Story: Gyudon can be served with various toppings and there are also a few different ways to make it (adding garlic etc.). You can eat Gyudon with beni shoga, Japanese seven spice blend (shichimi), with raw egg or soft boiled egg. There are Gyudon shops as fast food in every town in Japan and probably all Japanese people have eaten Gyudon.

 

Step 1
Cook rice (Wash and soak the rice in a bowl of water for 30 minutes. If cooking in a Kimono Mom Donabe, after it starts to boil, turn off the heat and leave for 15 – 20 minutes.)
 
Step 2
Slice the onion. Grate the red pickled ginger.
 
Step 3
To prevent the beef from overcooking and becoming tough, fry it separately and put it to one side.
 
Step 4
Add the onions to the pan along with the water and UMAMI SAUCE. Simmer until the onions have softened. Then add the cooked beef back into the pan.
 
Step 5
Plate the rice in a bowl and add the beef with some of the sauce on top. Finish with some red pickled ginger and serve hot!
 
 
Kimono Mom's Tips

The best ratio is 1:3 for Gyudon!

The red pickled ginger is optional if you can’t find it.

It tastes good to pour a little UMAMI SAUCE around the beef bowl when you eat it!

If you don’t eat beef, you can use other meat or even vegetables!

Credit to : https://kimonomom.com/recipe/beef-bowl/

title: Umami Sauce Udon
featured_image_alt: Umami Sauce Udon
content:
If udon noodles aren’t readily available in your country, here’s a recipe on how to make them from scratch! And also a delicious recipe on how to create a hot bowl of udon.

About Story:  Udon is a classic Japanese recipe that’s been eaten for hundreds of years. It’s a quick, relatively cheap and simple meal that when eaten with a hot soup it will be sure to warm you up! Udon noodles can also be eaten cold alongside a salad and a sauce. Some other examples of various udon dishes include Curry udon, Kitsune udon, Tempura udon, Oyako udon and Zaru udon.

 
 
 
1. Add 1 tsp salt and 150 ml water into a cup or measuring jug and mix so that the salt dissolves.

 

2. In a big bowl, place the 200g all-purpose flour and pour in the water little by little whilst constantly mixing.

 

3. Mix until a dough has formed and knead the dough. Shape into a ball, place into a bowl, cover it and then let the dough rest for 30 minutes.

 

4. To make the udon noodles, sprinkle some flour on the work surface and roll. Roll into a thin sheet. Fold the sheet into thirds on top of itself, turn the sheet horizontally and then cut vertically across so that long thin noodles are created. Cover the noodles in flour once again after cutting.

 

5. Boil the noodles in a pot of water for a few minutes then drain the water and cool them under running water.

 

6. You can serve the noodles and soup separately or add noodles to a bowl and then add the soup on top. If you choose to serve the noodles and soup together, serve quickly so that the udon doesn’t go soggy!

Notes

To knead the dough, sprinkle some flour on the surface first so that the dough doesn’t stick.

If the dough is too hard to roll, knead again and put a lot of flour on all surfaces.

Mix and boil together 50ml of UMAMI SAUCE and 300ml water. Boil with 1 serving  of udon noodles then take off the heat when the noodle have cooked and have become softer.

STEAK FAJITA PASTA WITH LOW-CARB SPAGHETTI

This pasta is low in carbs and is a delectable keto option that also caters to paleo, low-carb, Whole30, and gluten-free diets. It's a wonderfully satisfying bowl that's quick to prepare and offers a perfect blend of flavors.

 

Serve: 2

Recipe from It's Skinny Pasta

 

INGREDIENTS

1 package It's Skinny Spaghetti

1/2 onion, sliced

1/2 red and orange bell pepper, sliced

1 clove garlic, minced

1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped

2 tbsp olive oil

400g sirloin steak, cubed

1/4 cup chicken stock/broth (could also use beef broth)

1/8 tsp salt & pepper, to taste

 

DIRECTIONS

1. Drain your package of It’s Skinny Spaghetti, rinse, and set aside.

2. Thinly slice the onion, pepper, and garlic. Heat a skillet over medium-low heat, adding 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Saute the vegetables until tender. Add half the fresh parsley, remove the vegetables from the skillet, and set aside.

3. Add the sliced or cubed sirloin steak. Season the steak as desired. Add some chicken stock or broth (enough liquid to losen up the bits from the pan) and continue until the steak is cooked to your liking.

4. Return the fajita veggies to the skillet with the cooked steak. Add the remaining parsley and your package of It’s Skinny Spaghetti. Toss to combine. Allow the pasta to heat for 3-5 minutes, and you’re good to go! Sprinkle some more parsley on top of the pasta dish for color. Dish up and dig in!

INGREDIENTS

    1. Open one package of It’s Skinny Fettuccine. Drain, rinse, and set aside.
    2. Peel and cube your eggplant (save the other half for another of our yummy eggplant recipes). Lightly pat excess moisture from the eggplant with a paper towel. Chop the clove of garlic.
    3. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté the chopped garlic until fragrant. Add the cubed eggplant and season generously with salt and pepper. Saute the mixture until the eggplant becomes soft and tender, about 10-15 minutes.
    4. Add heavy cream to the pan and let it reduce into a thick sauce for about 5-8 minutes.
    5. Add the Fettuccine to your skillet, along with most of the grated parmesan cheese (save some for garnish). Toss the ingredients to combine. Let it cook until the noodles heat through, about 3-5 minutes.
    6. Dish up the eggplant alfredo in a bowl or plate and add the remaining Parmesan cheese to the top of the sauce. Dig in and enjoy this hearty and satisfying vegetarian meal!

title: Gymkhana Creamy Chicken Pies
featured_image_alt: Gymkhana Creamy Chicken Pies
content:
CREAMY CHICKEN PIES 

A marriage of the creaminess of the GYMKHANA butter masala sauce and the depth of the rogan josh sauce, this chicken pie is aromatic and delicious! Chicken marinated in Garlic and Chili Marinade then cooked with onions, garlic, ginger Simmered with rogan josh and butter masala sauces. Filled into puff pastry, folded, and baked until browned. Served with extra sauce to dip.

Recipe by Tara Maini

 

INGREDIENTS

4 Chicken Breasts

1 Jar Gymkhana Roasted Garlic and Chili Marinade

1 Onion, diced 1 tsp minced ginger

1 Jar Gymkhana Rogan Josh Cooking Sauce

1 Jar Gymkhana Butter Masala Cooking Sauce

445g Shortcrust pastry, defrosted (or Puff Pastry- whichever you prefer!)

1 Egg, whisked

Coriander bunch

Nigella seeds

 

STEPS

1. Cut 4 chicken breasts into bite-sized pieces.

2. Coat the chicken in 4 tbsp of the roasted garlic and chili marinade and set aside the marinate for 30 minutes.

3. Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the onions and saute until golden brown.

4. Add the ginger and chicken and cook for 5-6 minutes.

5. Pour in half a jar of Rogan Josh sauce. Simmer for 5 minutes before adding ½ a jar of Butter Masala Sauce, mix well. Simmer until the sauce has reduced to coat the chicken well.

6. Remove from the heat, and let cool.

7. Preheat the oven to 200. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.

8. Roll out the shortcrust pastry and cut out 5-6 inch rounds.

9. Once the filling is cooled, spoon about 2-3 tablespoons of filling onto one-half of each circle of pastry.

10. Brush the edges of the pastry with egg wash, then fold over and press to seal. Use a fork to press into the pastry to help seal further.

11. Repeat with the remaining pastry and filling then arrange on the baking tray.

12. Brush all the pies with egg. Sprinkle with nigella seeds.

13. Bake for 15-20 minutes, until the pastry is golden brown.

14. In a small pot over medium heat, mix the remaining ½ of each cooking sauce and simmer for 5 minutes to heat through.

15. Garnish with coriander and serve the pies with the sauce on the side to dip.

title: Kimchi Fried Rice
content:
Kimchi Fried Rice is a delicious Korean dish, that’s easy to make in just 15 minutes. You can serve it as a side dish or entree!

serving size: 1

INGREDIENTS:

  • 1 tbsp sesame oil

  • 1 cup onions, diced

  • 1 cup of Josun Hotel's Napa Kimchi, roughly chopped

  • 2 cloves garlic minced

  • 2 tbsp kimchi juice

  • 3 cups cooked rice If you don’t already have cooked rice available, be sure you start by cooking the rice.

  • ¼ cup soy sauce Tamari for gluten free

  • 1 tsp fresh garlic grated or ½ tsp ground ginger

  • 2 tbsp chili paste

 

OPTIONAL TOPPINGS

  • sesame seeds
  • green onions, diced

 

Instructions:

  1. Add the sesame oil to a large skillet over medium high heat.
  2. Add the onions and Josun Hotels Napa Kimchi, cook for 3-4 minutes, add the garlic and cook for an additional minute.
  3. Add the kimchi juice and bring to a simmer.
  4. Add the white rice, cook 1-2 minutes.
  5. Add the soy sauce, ginger and chili paste.
  6. Toss to combine, cook for an additional 3-4 minutes.

Top with sesame seeds and diced green onions if you would like.

Add-on options:

  • Top it with fried eggs. Fry eggs sunny side up in a separate skillet from the fried rice. Serve the eggs on top of the fried rice after plating it.
  • Add shrimp. Cooked shrimp can be added at the end. Or raw shrimp can be added with the veggies to cook in the skillet before adding the rice.
  • Add pork belly. Pork belly is a common ingredient found in kimchi fried rice. Add uncooked diced pork belly with the veggies to cook in the skillet before adding the rice. Or Add cooked diced pork belly at the end of cooking the fried rice.

title: Kimchi Pancake
content:
Kimchi pancake is easy and quick to make and is one of Koreans’ all time favorite dishes. It’s spicy, crispy, a little sweet and a little sour. 

Ingredients

  • 226g of Josun Hotel Napa Kimchi, chopped into small pieces, plus 2 tablespoons of the brine
  • 3 scallions, chopped
  • ½ teaspoon sugar
  • ½ cup all-purpose flour
  • ½ cup water
  • 4 tablespoons vegetable oil

 

Instructions

  1. Combine the kimchi, kimchi brine, scallions, sugar, flour, and water in a medium bowl and mix well with a spoon.
  2. Heat a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat. (If you don’t have a 12-inch skillet, use a smaller skillet to make 2 pancakes.)
  3. Add 2 tablespoons of the vegetable oil and swirl to coat the bottom of the pan.
  4. Pour the batter into the pan and spread it with the back of a spoon or a spatula to make a large circle.
  5. Cook until the bottom is golden brown and crisp, 3 to 5 minutes.
  6. Carefully turn the pancake over. Drizzle the remaining 2 tablespoons oil around the edges of the skillet, then lift the pancake with a thin spatula to allow the oil to run underneath and tilt the pan to spread it evenly.
  7. Cook until the bottom of the pancake is light golden brown and crisp, 3 to 5 minutes.
  8. Flip it one more time and cook for another minute.
  9. Slide onto a large serving platter and serve immediately.

title: Kimchi Grilled Cheese
content:
KIMCHI GRILLED CHEESE

by @meredithsflavourlibrary

 

Grilled cheese is one of the easiest and most versatile dishes, perfect for any meal—be it a quick lunch or a late-night indulgent supper.

The simplicity of a well-toasted bread filled with melted cheese is a timeless comfort food that never fails to satisfy. With the addition of kimchi, this classic dish transforms into a gourmet delight. The tanginess of kimchi not only cuts through the richness of the cheese, balancing flavours beautifully, but it also introduces a delightful crunch and a spicy kick. This combination makes it an excellent way to introduce kids to the unique taste of kimchi.

Renowned for their high-quality ingredients, Josun Hotel’s kimchi stands out with its rich, well-balanced flavours and authentic Korean taste. Kimchi, a traditional Korean fermented vegetable dish, is packed with numerous health benefits. Rich in probiotics, it aids digestion and promotes a healthy gut. Additionally, kimchi is low in calories but high in fibre and essential nutrients like vitamins A, B, and C. The fermentation process also enhances its antioxidant properties, making it a powerful addition to your diet. 

 

Whether you're looking for a quick meal or a new way to enjoy kimchi, this recipe is sure to satisfy both adults and kids alike.

 

Serves: 1

Prep time: 5 mins

Cook time: 10 mins

Ingredients:

- 2 slices of sourdough or your preferred bread

- 50 grams of sharp cheddar cheese (about 2 slices)

- 50 grams of provolone cheese (about 2 slices)

- 50 grams of comte cheese (about 2 slices)

- 30 grams of parmigiano cheese (grated)

- 80 grams of well-drained Josun Hotel Napa Cabbage kimchi, chopped 

- 14 grams of butter, softened (1 tablespoon)

- 20 grams of mayonnaise, (about 1.5 tablespoon)

 

Instructions:

  1. Drain kimchi well to remove excess moisture and chop into small pieces. 
  2. Lightly stir fry chopped up kimchi on a pan over medium heat for about 5 minutes.
  3. Spread butter on the one side of each bread slice.
  4. Combine kimchi and mayonnaise before spreading an even layer on the other side of each bread slice.
  5. Place both slices of bread, kimchi mayonnaise side down, on a preheated skillet or griddle over medium heat. 
  6. Grate parmigiano cheese over the buttered side of each bread before flipping both slices over.
  7. Layer the kimchi mayonnaise side with cheddar cheese, provolone cheese and comte cheese before closing both slices together.
  8. Cook until the bread is golden brown and the cheese starts to melt, about 3 - 4 minutes. Carefully flip the sandwich and continue cooking the other side until golden brown and the cheese is fully melted, another 3 - 4 minutes.
  9. Remove from the skillet, let it cool for a minute on a wire rack, then slice in half and enjoy your kimchi grilled cheese! Serve it with Little Farms’ homestyle roasted tomato and basil soup for a hearty well balanced meal.

title: Salted Caramel Vegan Protein Waffles
content:
When your waffles are both healthy and delicious, you can conquer anything in your day. Packed with goodness and our salted caramel protein powder, these are a must-make for your kitchen right away.

SERVING:

Makes 2 waffles 


Ingredients:

40g all-purpose flour

30g whole wheat flour 

20g white wolf nutrition salted caramel vegan protein blend

0.25 tsp baking soda

1 tsp baking powder

0.25 tsp cardamom

A pinch of salt

150g almond milk

5g white wine vinegar

Apples:
1 apple

½ tsp sugar

A pinch of salt

1tsp cinnamon

a splash of water

METHOD:

1. To make the waffles, combine all your dry ingredients in a bowl. Then add your almond milk and vinegar to a separate bowl and stir to combine.

2. Wait until the mix curdles before adding it in to the dry ingredients, fold until there’s no longer any dry flour visible in the bowl, a few lumps are okay.

3. Leave to rest while cooking up your apples.

4. Start by chopping your apple into cubes and adding it to a pan with your sugar, salt and cinnamon.

5. Add a splash of water and cook while stirring occasionally until the apples are tender.

6. Add more water as needed throughout the cooking process to prevent burning.

7. Preheat your waffle maker and grease it lightly with some oil or vegan butter.

8. Add in approximately half of your mixture (the amount needed will depend on the size of your waffle maker) and cook until done.

9. You can see that the waffle is done once there’s no longer any steam escaping from the sides of the waffle maker, then leave it in for a little while longer until it crisps up before removing the waffle.

10. Repeat until you’ve used up all your batter.

Plate up your waffles with your cooked apples, coconut yoghurt, berries and nut butter.

title: Pistachio Kunafa Chocolate Bar (Viral Dubai Chocolate)
content:
Staying with the times? Try our rendition of the Dubai Chocolate, this super easy and delicious Pistacho Chocolate Recipe will keep you wanting more!

Serves: 6

Prep time: 5 mins

Cook time: 10 mins

 

 Ingredients:

  • 100 g kataifi pastry thawed,
  • 2 tablespoon/ 30g  butter, melted
  • 1/2 cup pistachio butter
  • 200 g chocolate of choice, either chunks of Tony's, chips or broken up pieces of UP UP chocolate bars

 

Instructions:

      1. Chop the kataifi into 1/2 inch thick pieces, then place in a medium sized bowl and mix with the melted butter until well coated.
      2. Heat an air fryer to 350F (180C) , and line the basket of the air fryer with parchment paper.
      3. Add the shredded kataifi and air fry for 10 minutes, stirring every few minutes so that the kataifi toasts evenly.
      4. Alternately, you can add the kataifi to a large skillet over medium heat, and keep stirring until golden brown.
      5. Place the toasted kataifi into a large bowl, add the pistachio spread and stir well to combine.
      6. Set aside.
      7. Place the chopped chocolate in a microwave safe bowl.
      8. Microwave gently for 30 seconds, stir, then keep microwaving in 10 second bursts until the chocolate is just melted.
      9. Stir to smooth out any pieces.
      10. Line a 9×5 inch loaf pan with parchment paper, with an overhang so you can lift it out of the pan.
      11. Pour half the melted chocolate onto the base of the pan, so that it covers the bottom.
      12. Smooth out with a spoon until it forms an even layer.
      13. Place the loaf pan in the fridge to set for 5 minutes or until chocolate has hardened, then spoon all the pistachio kataifi mixture on top and spread to evenly cover the chocolate.
      14. Pour the remaining melted chocolate on top, smoothing out to cover evenly.
      15. Let the loaf pan set in the fridge for another 5-10 minutes.
      16. Once the chocolate has set, break it up into pieces like chocolate bark, don't worry about them being even.
      17. Enjoy immediately or store in the fridge!

title: Gut friendly Granola Bowl
content:
Looking for a balanced, gut friendly and super delicious granola bowl! We've got you covered!
 
Check out Raphaella's Instagram, @chickpeasandberries granola bowl recipe made with Little Farms breakfast range.
 
This Recipe is Rich in proteins, fibers and healthy fats for long lasting energy, providing Pro and Pre biotics to feed and develop good gut bacteria :) 
 
Recipe:
  1. Aim for approx 120 to 150 g yogurt,
  2. 2 tbsp of kefir,
  3. a good handful of berries and a small kiwi,
  4. 3 to 4 tbsp of granola,
  5. a few walnuts
  6. 1/2 tbsp of chia seeds
For the extra treat, drizzle a little raw honey and Enjoy !  
 
 
To find out more about the amazing nutrient benefits of this brekkie have a look below:
 
⁠Proteins:
•⁠  ⁠Choose a protein rich yogurt (min 10g / 100g)
Strained yogurt like this strained EVIA greek contain more protein and less sugar
Nb: if lactose intolerant, choose a lactose free version or go for a vegan yogurt ( less proteins though)
•⁠  ⁠Choose a granola rich in nuts and seeds with very little added unrefined sugar. Remember ingredients are listed from the most important one ! 
 
⁠Healthy fats:
Look out for unsaturated fats and avoid saturated ones or pro inflammatory oils like sunflower, soy, random vegetable oils mention.... 
I love the use of chia seeds (Omega 3 source/ anti inflammatory), Almonds ( Omega 6 and 3) and olive oil (Omega 9/ cardiovascular protection) in this granola. 
Adding walnuts which are the richest vegetal nut source of ALA Omega 3 and a tbsp of chia seeds, gives an extra boost !
 
⁠Feed your gut with Pro and prebiotics:
•⁠  ⁠Pro biotics are beneficial bacteria that can support your gut and overall health
By combining fermented milk like yogurt and kefir in this bowl, you get a variety of different good bacteria strains (up to 60 different strains in kefir !)
Ensure your yogurt and kefir feature the mention "live and alive cultures"
 
•⁠  ⁠Prebiotics is the food that feed the probiotics :) There are 3 categories: Soluble fibers, oligosaccharides and polyphenols
In this bowl: 
The oats contain betaglucane soluble fibers that have been proven to enhance good bacteria developments:)
Strawberries and  blueberries are loaded in polyphenols and the raw honey is also a great source !
As for kiwi its soluble fibers and polyphenols have been studied and definitely associated with feeding the good gut bacterias
 
Note: those fruits are also low in GI which is definitely better if you are going to start your day with a sweet breakfast to avoid too much of an insuline spike. 
And you get your daily dose of vitamin C at the same time in just one meal !

title: Butter Chicken Nachos
content:
Recipe by Tara @choperella

 

450g chicken breast
1 jar Gymkhana Classic Tandoori Marinade
1 jar GymKhana Butter Masala Cooking Sauce
300g salted tortilla chips
300g grated low-moisture mozzarella cheese
250g grated cheddar cheese
60g sour cream
2 roma tomatoes, seeded and chopped
1⁄2 red onion, finely diced
1 jalapeno, finely chopped (optional)
1⁄4 bunch of Cilantro leaves


1. Put the chicken breasts into a bowl and add one Gymkhana Classic Tandoori
marinade jar. Give it a good mix to coat. Let it sit for about 1 hour—up to 24 hours —
to marinate.
2. Preheat the oven to 200°C. Spray a roasting tin with oil or lay down parchment paper.
3. Once the chicken has marinated, place it on the prepared tin and pop it into the oven.
Roast for 18-20 minutes, basting and flipping halfway.
4. Once the chicken is cooked, let it cool down slightly. Shred the chicken and set aside
using two forks or your trusty hands and add to a bowl.
5. Toss the chicken with 3⁄4 of the Gymkhana butter masala sauce.
6. Lower the oven to 180°C. Arrange one even layer of nacho chips on a baking tray
lined with parchment paper. Sprinkle on half the cheese and scatter half of the
chicken.
7. Repeat with the remaining nachos, cheese, and chicken, and then pop the tray in the
oven. Bake for 6-8 minutes, until the cheese has melted and the chips begin to toast.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining butter masala sauce in a small saucepan.
8. When nachos are done, drizzle with sour cream and top them with chopped onions,
tomatoes, jalapenos, and coriander.
9. Serve with the butter masala sauce on the side to dip, enjoy!

title: Chilli Honey and Harissa Slow-Cooked Lamb
featured_image_title: Chilli Honey and Harissa Slow-Cooked Lamb
content:
Chilli Honey and Harissa Slow-Cooked Lamb

Recipe by Karlie Verkerk

Cooking time: 5 hours

Serves: 12-14 as part of a shared meal

 

 

INGREDIENTS

200g (about 8) gold shallots, peeled and halved lengthways

1 head garlic, halved 

1 bone-in lamb leg or shoulder (about 1.8kg)

500ml chicken or vegetable stock

1½ tbsp chilli honey (or regular honey if you prefer mild)

1 lemon, halved

SPICE RUB

1 tbsp fennel seeds

2 garlic cloves

1½ tbsp harissa powder

2 tbsp olive oil

2 tsp sea salt flakes

 

METHOD

  1. To make the spice rub, combine fennel and garlic in a mortar and pestle and pound to create a paste. Add remaining ingredients and stir to combine; set aside. Alternatively, you can make the spice rub in a small food processor or blender.
  2. Preheat the oven to 160°C fan-forced. Place shallots and garlic in a large baking tray, then place the lamb leg or shoulder over the top. Use a sharp knife to score the top side of the lamb, on an angle about 1cm apart. Don’t slice too deep, just 5mm will do. 
  3. Spoon over spice rub, then use your hands to massage it into the meat. Fill the tray with stock, cover tightly with aluminium foil, then transfer lamb to the oven for 4 hours, or until meat pulls away from the bone easily.
  4. Once lamb is fall-apart tender, remove lamb from oven and discard foil; drizzle over honey, then return to the oven for a further 20 minutes or until skin is caramelised. 
  5. To make charred lemon, preheat a frying pan over medium-high heat. Place lemon, flesh-side down on the pan, and cook until starting to blacken. Serve with lamb.

title: What Are Bovaer Feed Additives?
content:
Are Bovaer Feed Additives in Your Food?

At Little Farms, we pride ourselves on being transparent about what’s in the food we sell. This transparency is backed by rigorous standards, including our banned ingredients list, which prohibits over 200 additives and preservatives. One question that has recently come up is about Bovaer feed additives — what they are, whether they are harmful, and if the meat at Little Farms, such as Bostock Brothers Chicken, Green Meadows, Greenwood Valley, and Mount Barker products, contains them.

What Are Bovaer Feed Additives?

Bovaer is a feed additive designed to reduce methane emissions from livestock. Methane is a potent greenhouse gas, and ruminant animals like cows and sheep are significant contributors to its release through digestion processes. By adding Bovaer to animal feed, it suppresses an enzyme in the stomachs of livestock, reducing the production of methane. This technology is considered a potential solution to lowering the carbon footprint of the meat and dairy industry.

Why Could Bovaer Be Harmful?

While Bovaer is hailed as an innovative solution for mitigating climate change, there are concerns surrounding its use. Critics argue that its long-term effects on animal health and the ecosystem are not yet fully understood. Additionally, consumers are increasingly wary of chemical additives in any form, even if they are designed with good intentions. At Little Farms, we believe that the integrity and natural quality of our food should never be compromised by additives, even those aimed at addressing environmental concerns.

Does Little Farms’ Meat Contain Bovaer?

We’re proud to confirm that the meat products at Little Farms, including Bostock Brothers Chicken, Green Meadows beef, Greenwood Valley lamb, and Mount Barker chicken, do not contain Bovaer or any other artificial feed additives. These brands align with our commitment to offering natural, ethically sourced, and minimally processed products. They are raised on feed that meets stringent standards, ensuring their quality and safety.

The Little Farms Difference

Choosing Little Farms means you can trust what’s on your plate. Our suppliers share our dedication to ethical farming practices, transparency, and avoiding unnecessary additives. This commitment is why you’ll find Bostock Brothers Chicken raised on organic pastures, Green Meadows beef from grass-fed and finished cattle, Greenwood Valley lamb that’s pasture-raised, and Mount Barker chicken that’s free-range and free from antibiotics and artificial growth promoters.

Little Farms Promise: Your Health, Our Priority

We understand that what you eat matters — to your health, the environment, and the future of farming. That’s why we continually review our products and suppliers to ensure they meet our high standards. With Little Farms, you’re not just buying groceries; you’re investing in a healthier, more sustainable future.

Have more questions about what’s in your food? Visit us in-store or contact our team at info@littlefarms.com to learn more. At Little Farms, we’re always here to help you make informed choices.

title: Little Farms Sentosa Opens Its Doors, Completing the Perfect Picture of Island Living in Singapore
content:
Little Farms Sentosa Opens Its Doors, Completing the Perfect Picture of Island Living in Singapore

- The launch of the brand’s seventh retail outlet and sixth restaurant; bringing Little Farms’ commitment to all- natural, organic produce to one of Singapore’s most scenic waterfront locations
- An extensive retail offering that comprises its franchise defining premium fresh produce, Little Farms Butchery, a Cheese & Deli Counter and Grab & Go items and a wide range of artisanal wines
- Inspired by the sea, the Table by Little Farms Sentosa restaurant adds a range of exclusive seafood dishes to be enjoyed on its outdoor terrace overlooking the marina
- Little Farms, Later provides a series of nighttime offers to bring the community together - kids eat free after 5pm on Sundays, 1-for-1 Small Plates every Tuesday, daily Happy Hour - and more

 

SINGAPORE, 2 DECEMBER 2024 — Little Farms Sentosa has opened its doors, bringing the brand’s commitment to all-natural, organic produce to one of Singapore’s most scenic waterfront locations. Completing the perfect picture of island living, this newly renovated space seamlessly integrates a grocery store and restaurant to meet the needs of the discerning local community. Set to elevate both daily living and special moments, Little Farms Sentosa offers the highest quality fresh ingredients to cook at home, healthy grab-and-go options, and an all-day dining experience at Table by Little Farms.

 

As is the case at every Little Farms outlet, shoppers and diners can trust that every item they purchase, or order is not only nutritious and clean but also of the highest quality. Sourcing through the brand’s network of ethical suppliers, each product undergoes rigorous checks against its banned ingredient list, which excludes over 200 harmful chemicals, artificial additives, and preservatives, ensuring only the purest, healthiest options make it to their plate.

Joe Stevens, CEO of Little Farms, shares his excitement at the brand’s expansion to the island, “We asked our customers where they would like Little Farms to open next and Sentosa emerged as one of the top locations. We are delighted to be here! We have always loved the Sentosa community, as friends and customers, and are excited about our new stunning waterfront location. We’re thrilled to bring our all natural, healthy and delicious food to Sentosa. Thanks for the warm welcome we’ve received so far, and we look forward to being an active member of the community.”

 

Table by Little Farms Sentosa
Measuring over 3,000 square feet, Table by Little Farms Sentosa boasts a live open kitchen and an expansive alfresco terrace with views of the marina below. With a menu as wholesome as it is delicious, hearty breakfast favourites include the B.L.A.T.E - featuring a freshly baked Starter Lab brioche bun filled with nitrate- free bacon, lettuce, avocado, tomato, egg, cheddar and homemade BBQ sauce - which is paired with healthier staples like the Organic Açai Bowl with granola, banana, strawberry, mango and coconut. Fresh and lighter main dishes such as the Avocado, Quinoa and Feta Bowl with walnut, blueberry, tomato, baby spinach, baby romaine, pomegranate, miso and lemon sit alongside satisfying favourites including the Smash Burger with Australian O’Connor Beef, cheese, sriracha mayo and fries. Vibrant Asian ingredients come to the fore with dishes such as the Rendang Lamb Shank with a quinoa “Ulam” rice, potato and pickled onion and the Organic Chicken & Cauliflower Rice using Bostock Brothers Fresh Organic Chicken from New Zealand, romaine salad, almond chilli pesto, ginger and coriander.

 

Sentosa Exclusive Dishes & Drinks
Set to become a favourite amongst the Sentosa community are the Sourdough Flatbread Pizzas with premium toppings such as Garlic Prawn & Avocado with broccoli, kale, gremolata, parmesan and garlic cream or Italian Sausage with fennel, scallion, green chilli, mozzarella and stewed plum tomatoes.

 Inspired by its waterfront location, the menu will also play home to some exclusive seafood dishes. The Prawn Brioche Roll features sustainably sourced Selva shrimp dressed in a housemade curry aioli and served with dill in a Starter Lab brioche roll with fries. Dinner specials, available from 5pm onwards, include ⁠Citrus Cured Akaroa Salmon with calamansi, rye cracker, arugula, pickled cucumber and dill cream cheese and Poached Red Snapper in Sencha Sake Broth, served with clams, puffed rice, pickled radish and toasted sesame.

Introducing two tropical additions to the Little Farms Sentosa menu: the Coconut Shake, a refreshing blend of coconut ice cream, coconut water, coconut flesh, beetroot, and desiccated coconut; and Cloudy Sunshine, a mix of orange cream, whipped cream, orange juice, milk, espresso, and a touch of maple syrup.

Little Farms, Later

Little Farms, Later extends the Little Farms love into golden hour and beyond with a series of nighttime offers to bring the community together. On Tuesdays, guests can enjoy 1-for-1 small plates while unwinding with their favourite sundowners. Wednesdays feature the perfect midweek treat - a Smash Burger paired with a refreshing Dingo Lager for just $30. Thirsty Thursdays offers an all-day happy hour, with $8 beers, $10 wines by the glass, and $12 cocktails. And on Sundays, after 5pm, kids eat free, making it the ideal way to enjoy a family meal together.

 

Deli Counter: Cheese & Charcuterie Platters Made to Order

Designed with entertainers and boat parties in mind, the deli counter at Little Farms Sentosa is a heavenly display of quality, all-natural, organic produce. Dedicated cheesemongers are on hand to curate the perfect platters for any occasion, offering rustic cheeses including Aged Gouda, Tête de Moine, Camembert, and Brie de Meaux, all sourced directly from Rungis Market in Paris. Charcuterie favourites such as Parma Ham, Serrano Ham, and Bayonne Ham are thoughtfully selected from independent farmers and suppliers, ensuring only the finest offerings for every gathering.

Little Farms Butchery
Behind every cut at The Butchery at Little Farms is a backstory of careful sourcing, sustainability, and exceptional quality. Each premium meat is handpicked from trusted farms, where ethical practices and expert craftsmanship come together to deliver the finest flavours to your table. Each cut is more than just premium – it’s part of a tradition of excellence.

 

Commonly recognised as Australia’s finest beef, O'Connor Beef is entirely free-range, and raised on Gippsland's crisp fresh air, pristine water and nutrient-rich pure pastures without any artificial hormones or antibiotics. Little Farms proudly sells Roaring Forties Lamb, named after the strong westerly winds, driven by oceanic storms from Antarctica. These winds, which carry the cleanest air as recorded at Cape Grim, create

a temperate climate that supports the lush, fertile lands of Southern Victoria and Tasmania, making it ideal for premium lamb production. Little Farms also serves as the exclusive retailer of Bostock Brothers Fresh Organic Chicken from New Zealand, a premium product known for its exceptional quality and ethical farming practices, ensuring the birds are healthier and more naturally raised. The result is tender, flavourful meat that is rich in taste and nutrients.

Grab & Go

Little Farms understands the importance of convenience and simplicity in navigating the demands of everyday life. While ready meals are often associated with additives and preservatives, Little Farms Ready Meals stand apart, made with only the finest, all-natural ingredients for a truly exceptional dining experience. The Grab & Go counter will include a range of freshly made salad bowls, ready-to-heat-meals and hearty soups.

Joy Bottled: Excellent Value Wines & Spirits

Over the past three years, Little Farms has worked on expanding its portfolio of wines sourced directly from the vineyard. Now, over 75% of the wine range comes directly from the cellar door, ensuring both quality and value for money. These wines can be enjoyed at store price within Table by Little Farms.

Fresh Bakes from Starter Lab

Little Farms' in-house bakery, Starter Lab, will be offering a range of freshly baked items at their Sentosa store, including best-selling sourdough, croissants, pain au chocolat, focaccia, and baguettes.

Little Farms Market and Table by Little Farms are now open at Sentosa. Little Farms Market is open daily from 7:30am to 10pm, providing a wide range of organic and all-natural products. Table by Little Farms welcomes guests Monday to Tuesday from 7:30am to 5:00pm and Wednesday to Sunday from 7.30am to 10:00pm, where you can indulge in a variety of delicious, freshly prepared dishes.

title: Panettone Bread and Butter Pudding
content:
Panettone Bread and Butter Pudding 

Recipe by Karlie Verkerk

Cook time: 40 minutes

Serves: 6

 

INGREDIENTS

1 panettone (about 750gm)

2 eggs

1¼ cups milk

⅓ cup double cream

2 tbsp caster sugar

1 tsp vanilla bean paste

Finely grated zest from ½ an orange

Pinch of salt

Butter, for greasing

Icing sugar, to serve

Vanilla ice-cream, to serve

 

METHOD

  1. Preheat the oven to 180°C. Cut panettone into 3cm cubes and set aside.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine eggs, milk, cream, sugar, vanilla, orange zest and salt; whisk to dissolve sugar.
  3. Add panettone to custard mixture and stir gently to combine; set aside for 2 minutes to allow the bread to soak up the liquid. Meanwhile, grease a large baking dish or individual ramekins with butter. Transfer pudding mixture to baking dish, then bake for 20-30 minutes or until top is golden and the custard mixture is just set. 
  4. Serve hot with a scoop of ice-cream and a sprinkle of icing sugar.

title: Abalone Sizzling Chicken Pot Recipe
content:
Abalone Sizzling Chicken Pot Recipe


Ingredients:
•    1 LF free-range chicken (800g)
•    4 piece abalones (1 can)
•    A large piece of ginger
•    6 shallots
•    2 heads of garlic
•    Half a stalk of spring onion
•    Fresh coriander (for garnish)
•    Cooking oil (as needed)
•    1 teaspoon salt
•    2 tablespoons soy sauce/Organic sauce - Shoyu
•    2 tablespoons Umami sauce
•    2 tablespoons rice wine
•    A pinch of sugar
•    1 tablespoon oyster sauce/Hoisin sauce 
•    1 tablespoon cornstarch


Method:
Step 1: Prepare the ingredients: Choose a tender chicken suitable for stir-frying and braising, such as free-range chicken or native chicken. For the abalone, use LF seasonal can.
Step 2: For the chicken: Cut into pieces and marinate with 1 tablespoon of rice wine, salt, sugar, soy sauce or Shoyu, oyster sauce or Hoisin, Umami, cornstarch, and some oil. Let it marinate for half an hour.
For the abalone: Just open it and cut with pattern. 
Step 3: Slice the ginger into thick pieces, slightly crush the garlic, cut the spring onion into 3-inch sections, and peel the shallots.
Step 4: Heat oil in a wok to around 60% heat, then add the ginger, garlic, shallots, and spring onion. Stir-fry on medium-high heat until they slightly change color and release their aroma. Once done, arrange the ingredients at the bottom of the wok.
Step 5: Place the marinated chicken pieces evenly on top of the ginger, garlic, shallots, and spring onion. Ensure they are spread out uniformly, then cover the wok with a lid.
Step 6: Turn the heat to medium and braise for 8-10 minutes.
Step 7: Place the abalone on top of the chicken pieces, cover the wok again, and cook for another 3-5 minutes.
Step 8: Finally, remove the lid, turn the heat to high, pour in the remaining rice wine, sprinkle with fresh coriander, and serve!

title: BBQ Mussel Paella
content:
Bringing the flavors of the sea to your table with this hearty paella, made even better with fresh Forsyth Island mussels. Follow the steps below to create a rich, flavorful dish packed with smoky spices and vibrant ingredients.

Ingredients:

70ml canola oil  
250g white onion, finely peeled and chopped  
30g garlic, crushed  
10g turmeric  
20g smoked paprika  
350g carnaroli rice  
800ml chicken stock  
and the juice from the mussel pouches  
3 bay leaves  
350g tomatoes, chopped finely  
2kg forsyth island mussels  
150g chorizo, diced  
160g whole roasted capsicum, drained and sliced  
140g baby peas, frozen  
season with salt, pepper, and parsley  

Method:

  1. Heat oil in a paella pan or high-sided pan.
  2. Add chopped onion and cook on medium for 4-5 minutes, then add garlic and cook for a further couple of minutes until soft.
  3. Add spices and bay leaves and cook for another 2 minutes, then add the tomatoes.
  4. Add all the rice evenly into the pan, then add the chicken and mussel stock, spreading evenly. Cook on medium-low heat, allowing the rice grains to soften and absorb the liquid.
  5. Once the liquid is absorbed and the rice has softened, add the chorizo, peppers, peas, and mussels. Let the mussels heat through.
  6. Season with salt and pepper, and garnish with parsley.

title: Creamy White Wine and Garlic Mussel Broth
content:
Indulge in a rich and flavorful dish featuring fresh Forsyth Island mussels, steamed in a fragrant broth of white wine, garlic, and herbs. Finished with a touch of cream and served with toasted ciabatta, this dish is perfect for a cozy meal with a glass of wine.

Ingredients:

  • 1 Kg Forsyth Mussels
  • 4 X Shallots Thinly Sliced
  • 1 X Cup Dry White Wine
  • ¾ Cup Chicken Stock
  • ½ Cup Heavy Cream
  • 8 X Cloves Garlic Diced Finely
  • 1/3 Cup Freshly Chopped Parsley
  • 1 X Tbsp Butter
  • 1 X Tbsp Olive Oil
  • 1 X Tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice
  • 1/3 Cup Lemon Zest Lemon Wedges for Serving
  • Toasted Ciabatta for Serving
  • Salt & Pepper to taste

Method:

  1. Begin by prepping your forsyth mussels and remove any beards.
  2. In a large pan, heat butter and oil and add the finely chopped shallots and garlic. Sauté until fragrant.
  3. Add the lemon juice and lemon zest, then stir to combine. Add the mussels, white wine, and chicken stock.
  4. Stir well to coat all mussels. Place the lid over the pan and keep the heat on medium. Over 6-8 minutes, leave the mussels to steam and open. Reduce the heat and slowly pour in the cream, stirring as you go.
  5. Allow to simmer for an additional 3-4 minutes. While the mussels are simmering in the sauce, toast your ciabatta with a little olive oil on a hot pan. Finish by adding salt, pepper, and parsley to the mussels.
  6. Serve with a large lemon wedge and more parsley, depending on your taste. Enjoy with a glass of white wine!

title: Chocolate Lava Cake
content:
Spice up your Valentine’s Day with the ultimate indulgence—warm, gooey Chocolate Lava Cake! With its rich, molten center and irresistible flavor, this dessert is pure romance on a plate. Perfect for sharing with your loved ones and guaranteed to make hearts melt. Ready to bake? Let’s get started!


Ingredients

6 ounces (170g) semi-sweet chocolate
1/2 cup (8 Tbsp; 113g) unsalted butter
1/4 cup (31g) all-purpose flour (spooned & leveled)
1/2 cup (60g) confectioners’ sugar/ icing sugar
1/8 teaspoon salt
2 large eggs
2 large egg yolks

optional toppings: ice cream, berries, and/or chocolate syrup

Instructions

    1. Preheat oven to 425°F (218°C). Spray four 6-ounce ramekins or six muffin cups with nonstick spray and dust with cocoa powder.
    2. Microwave butter and chopped chocolate in 10-second intervals, stirring until smooth.
    3. In a small bowl, whisk together flour, confectioners’ sugar or icing sugar, and salt. In another bowl, whisk eggs and yolks. Combine both mixtures with chocolate, stirring until smooth.
    4. Divide batter evenly into ramekins or muffin cups.
    5. Place ramekins on a baking sheet and bake for 12–14 minutes (8–10 minutes for muffin cups) until edges are firm but centers are soft.
    6. Cool for 1 minute. Invert onto plates using oven mitts; cakes should release easily.
    7. Add toppings and serve immediately.

title: Summer Peach Tart
content:
Summer Peach Tart Recipe – A Slice of Sunshine! ????

Celebrate the sweetness of summer with this vibrant Summer Peach Tart, a perfect dessert to enjoy on warm sunny days. With a buttery, flaky crust and a luscious peach filling, this tart is bursting with the fresh, juicy flavor of ripe peaches.  Whether you're hosting a summer gathering or simply treating yourself, this tart is a showstopper that's easy to make and even easier to enjoy.

Try it today and add a little sunshine to your table!

INGREDIENTS:

SWEET PASTRY
350 g (2 3/4 cup) flour
Large pinch kosher salt
150 g (11 Tbsp) unsalted butter, cold and diced
100 g (3/4 cup) powdered sugar
2 eggs, lightly beaten

Egg Wash
1 egg, beaten

PEACHES
4 peaches (~700 g), cored and sliced thin 
1/4 cup granulated sugar
2 tsp almond extract
1 lemon, juice of

CUSTARD
500 ml (2 cups) full-fat milk 
1 Tbsp butter
2 tsp vanilla extract
2 eggs
1 1/2 tsp corn starch
1/4 cup sugar 

ASSEMBLY
2 Tbsp apricot or peach jam
Toppings, optional
•⁠  ⁠blueberries or blackberries
•⁠  ⁠Mint leaves 

 

INSTRUCTIONS:

1.⁠ ⁠Whisk the flour and salt in a large bowl. Add the butter. Cut with a pastry cutter until fine crumbs form. Mix in the powdered sugar and eggs. Bring together to form a dough. Wrap with cling film and refrigerate 30 mins.

 2.⁠ ⁠Preheat oven to 180 C / 350 F.

 3.⁠ ⁠In a bowl, gently toss around the peach slices, sugar, almond extract and lemon juice so the peaches get evenly coated.

 4.⁠ ⁠For the custard, add the milk, butter and vanilla to a pan over medium heat until it comes to a simmer, stirring. 

 5.⁠ ⁠In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, corn starch and sugar until the sugar dissolves.

 6.⁠ ⁠Place the pan containing the milk mixture back over medium heat and gradually add in the eggs mixture, whisking continuously. Cook over low heat for ~5-10 mins, or until the mixture thickens and coats the back of a wooden spoon. Set aside. 

 7.⁠ ⁠Roll out the pastry dough to fit a buttered 22 cm (8 1/2 in) removable bottom pastry tin. Brush the rims with the egg wash. Prick with a fork and blind bake for 10 mins.

 8.⁠ ⁠Add the custard filling, spreading it out even. Arrange the peach slices, skin side up, in two rows in tight formation to fill the pastry.

 9.⁠ ⁠Bake for 25-30 mins until the peaches are nicely roasted and the custard is firm.

10.⁠ ⁠Remove from the oven and let cool slightly. For the glaze, brush the peaches with the jam. Garnish with berries of choice and/ or mint leaves (optional) before serving.

title: Creamy Miso Garlic Tofu
content:
This creamy miso garlic tofu is packed with flavor and makes a perfect weeknight meal! By blending Everiday Foods Miso Garlic Chili Oil with peanut butter or tahini, you get a quick, delicious dish that highlights tofu’s ability to absorb bold flavors.

Preparation time: 10 min

Cooking time: 10 min

Total time: 20 min

 

INGREDIENTS:

 

Tofu
  • 600g organic firm tofu
  • 4 cups hot water +3 Tbsp salt
  • spray oil
  • 2 Tbsp tapioca or arrowroot flour
Sauce
  • 2 Tbsp Everiday Miso Garlic Chili Oil
  • 2 Tbsp Everiday Coconut Aminos
  • 2 Tbsp tahini or peanut butter
  • 2 Tbsp black vinegar or rice vinegar
  • 2 Tbsp wate
Optional Garnish
  • toasted sesame seeds
  • spring onions
  • cilantro

INSTRUCTIONS

  1. Preheat oven or air fryer to 200℃ / 380℉
  2. Soak your tofu in the hot water with salt for 15 minutes
  3. Remove the tofu from the salt water and pat with a kitchen towel to remove as much moisture as possible.
  4. Cut the tofu into 1-inch pieces. Spray with oil and sprinkle with tapioca or arrowroot flour, and toss to coat.
  5. Airfry for for ~20 minutes or bake for ~40 minutes or until browned.
  6. While your tofu is cooking, mix your sauce ingredients together.
  7. Once your tofu is ready, heat a pan on a medium flame. Add your sauce and heat through.  
  8. Add your tofu and toss to coat. Add a little water if needed and cook till for 3 to 5 minutes.
  9. Plate your tofu and garnish.
  10. Serve with a side of greens and rice.

title: Labneh Chili Crisp Dip
content:
A delicious dip perfect for snacking or entertaining

An unexpected combination that just works! The cool, creamy labneh pairs beautifully with fresh lemon zest and juice, savory chili crisp, and a touch of honey for those who love a sweet-savory balance.

Preparation time: 5 min

Total time: 5 min

INGREDIENTS

  • 1 cup labneh
  • zest of half a lemon
  • juice of 1/4 lemon
  • 1 to 2 Tbsp (or more)  Everiday Chili Crisp
  • chopped scallions
  • drizzle of honey (optional)
  • flakey seasalt (optional but recommended if your labneh is unsalted)

INSTRUCTIONS

  1. Spread your Labneh out on a flat plate in an even layer

  5. Add a drizzle of honey.  This is optional, I know some don't like the whole sweet/savoury combo
  6. Add a pinch of flaky sea salt.  Also optional but recommended if your labneh isn't salted 
  7. Finish by garnishing with fresh chopped spring onion
  8. Serve with sliced cucumbers, Everiday gluten-free pita, or your favorite chips.

title: Gluten-Free Korean Marinated Mayak Eggs
content:
An Everiday rendition of the classic Korean Marinated Eggs

These gluten-free Korean marinated eggs (Mayak eggs) deliver bold, umami-rich flavors without soy, thanks to a coconut aminos-based marinade. With jammy yolks soaked in a savory-sweet blend of Everiday garlic chili oil, rice vinegar, and sesame, they make an irresistible addition to any meal!

Preparation time: 5 min
Cooking time: 6 min
Waiting time: 10 min
Total time: 21 min

INGREDIENTS

  • 6 eggs
  • 1/3 cup coconut aminos
  • 1/4 cup rice vinegar
  • 1 Tbsp sesame oil
  • 1/3 cup water
  • 1 red or green bird-eye chili, thinly sliced (optional)
  • 3 scallions, chopped,
  • 1 Tbsp Everiday garlic chili oil
  • 2 cloves of garlic, chopped
  • 1 Tbsp toasted sesame seeds

INSTRUCTIONS:

  1. Bring a large pot of water to a boil.  Once boiling, gently lower each egg into the pot and set a timer for 6 minutes for room temperature eggs or 7 minutes for cold eggs. 
  2. While the eggs are cooking, make the marinade by mixing all the res of the ingredients in a bowl and set aside.
  3. Once the eggs are done cooking, place the eggs in an ice bath to stop cooking. Once cooled, you can peel them.  If I am not in a rush, I like to let the eggs come up to room temperature.  I find them easier to peel this way.
  4. Add the eggs in a container and pour the marinade on top. For best flavor, let it marinate overnight in the fridge.
  5. Serve, the egss,cut in half over rice and drizzle some of the marinade liquid on top.

title: Persian Ground Meat and Potato Patties
content:
A truly authentic Persian dish, kotlets made with tender ground lamb or beef and russet potatoes offer a deliciously crispy crust and a soft, delicate interior that will leave you craving more!

 

Ingredients

1 1/2 pounds (680 g) russet potatoes, peeled, cut in 2-inch chunks, and rinsed under cold running water

Kosher salt

4 large eggs

1 pound (450 g) ground beef, ground lamb, or a combination

1 teaspoon ground turmeric

1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper

All-purpose flour, for dusting the patties

Extra-virgin olive oil, neutral oil, or a combination, for pan-frying

 

 

Method & Equipment

  • Prepare the Potatoes:

    • Peel and cut into 2-inch chunks.
    • Wash before boiling to remove surface starch.
    • Rinse after boiling to prevent gumminess.
    • Mash until smooth using a ricer or food mill (avoid a food processor to prevent a gummy texture).

  • Mixing Ingredients:

    • Combine all ingredients except mashed potatoes first.
    • Add mashed potatoes after other ingredients are mixed to avoid scrambling the eggs.

  • Portioning & Forming Patties:

    • Scoop the mixture into 50g portions before forming patties.
    • Shape patties one at a time, placing each into the skillet before making the next.
    • This prevents the flour from absorbing moisture and ensures proper crisping.
    • Slowing the addition of patties helps maintain oil temperature.

  • Prevent Ballooning:

    • Slightly dimple each patty (about 1/8 inch deep) with the back of a spoon before frying.

  • Pan-Frying Tips:

    • Gently shake the pan occasionally to distribute oil evenly.
    • Helps with even browning and prevents sticking.

title: Stuffed Samosas
content:
Samosas originated in Persia and are now popular worldwide, known for their crispy, golden pastry filled with spiced potatoes and peas. This recipe keeps it simple—flavourful filling, flaky dough, and a perfect crunch in every bite!


Ingredients

For the Pastry Dough:
2 cups (280 g) all-purpose flour and extra for shaping and rolling out the pastry
1 1/2 teaspoons salt
1 teaspoons caraway seeds, lightly cracked (optional)
1/4 cup (60 ml) neutral oil, such as avocado oil
1/3 cup plus 3 tablespoons (80 ml plus 45 ml) chilled water, divided

For the Potato and Pea Filling:
1 1/2 pounds (680 g) medium russet potatoes, cleaned and scrubbed
a pinch of salt
1/2 cup (60 g) frozen peas, thawed and drained
2 tablespoons (30 ml) neutral oil, such as avocado oil
2 teaspoons ground coriander
1 teaspoon cumin seeds
1 teaspoon ground turmeric
1/2 teaspoon garam masala
1/2 teaspoon Kashmiri chile powder 
1 teaspoon ground black pepper
1 to 2 fresh green chiles such as jalapeño stemmed and finely chopped
1 (2-inch; 5 cm) piece fresh ginger, peeled and minced
1/4 cup (15 g) tightly packed chopped fresh cilantro leaves and tender stems
mint or cilantro for serving
 

Directions:

  1. For the Pastry Dough: In the bowl of a stand mixer, combine flour, salt, and caraway seeds (if using) and mix by hand to evenly disperse the ingredients. Drizzle oil over the flour and rub it in with your fingertips. Once the fat is completely incorporated into the flour, the mixture will take on a crumbly appearance.
  2. Set bowl on stand mixer, and fit with dough hook attachment. Add 1/3 cup (80ml) of chilled water and mix on low speed until dough comes together in a ball, adding extra water 1 tablespoon (15ml) at a time as needed to form a cohesive dough; it should not be unduly sticky or wet, nor should it be dry and crumbly. Stop the mixer, scrape down sides of bowl with a rubber spatula, then continue to knead on low speed until dough is smooth and slightly elastic to the touch, pliable and resistant to tearing, but not tough, about 5 minutes. 
  3. The dough should weigh about 1 pound (455g). Wrap dough in plastic, and let it rest at cool room temperature, around 70°F (21°C), until dough is pliable, and jumps back when gently pressed, at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours. For a longer rest, it can be refrigerated for up to 24 hours, then brought to cool room temperature, around 70°F (21°C), before use.
  4. For the Potato and Pea Filling: Place potatoes in a medium saucepan, cover with enough water so they are fully submerged, and add 1 teaspoon (4g) salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, reduce heat to a simmer, cover with a lid, and cook until potatoes are tender, offering little resistance when poked with a paring knife, about 20 minutes. Drain potatoes and allow to cool until easy to handle; wipe out saucepan and return to stovetop.
  5. Once cool, peel and discard skins, and transfer potatoes to a large bowl. Using a fork, mash potatoes until flaky and no visible chunks remain, about 1 minute. The texture should not resemble smooth mashed potatoes. Add peas and stir gently to combine.
  6. In now-empty saucepan, heat oil over medium heat until shimmering. Add coriander, cumin, turmeric, and garam masala, and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, 30 to 45 seconds. Remove from heat and add chile powder.
  7. Pour contents of saucepan over potato mixture. Add black pepper, green chiles, ginger, cilantro, and 1 teaspoon (4g) salt. Using a rubber spatula, fold until well combined. Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt if needed.
  8. If making samosas right away, let filling cool to room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C), before using. Alternatively, transfer filling to an airtight container and refrigerate until ready to use. Allow to come to room temperature before stuffing into dough.
  9. For Filling, Frying and Serving the Samosas: Divide dough into 10 equal portions by weight, and shape each into a ball over a cool and dry surface using minimal flour. Transfer dough balls to a lightly floured baking sheet and cover loosely with plastic wrap. Fill a small bowl with water.
  10. Working with one ball of dough at a time, roll out dough to form a 7-inch (17cm) circle. Using a sharp knife, cut the circle in half; return to the baking sheet. Repeat with remaining dough balls.
  11. Working with one semicircle at a time, wet a fingertip in the bowl of water and dab halfway down the straight edge, and then fold the wet end over the dry side, pressing gently to seal. This will form a triangular pocket. Hold the pocket open like a little waffle cone, and gently spoon in 40g (about 3 tablespoons) potato filling. Dab the tip of a finger in water and moisten the inner flap of dough, then fold it over the filling, and press gently to seal it against the dough on the other side, then gently pinch each corner of the samosa to ensure all three points are well sealed.
  12. Transfer samosa to a lightly floured baking sheet and cover loosely with plastic wrap. Repeat the process with remaining dough and filling. Prior to frying, if the dough seems to have warmed up too much and feels too soft, briefly refrigerate samosas until dough is just firm. (If allowed to chill completely, the interiors may not properly cook through.)
  13. Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 200°F (95°C). Set a wire rack in a rimmed baking sheet, and set aside. In a large Dutch oven, add enough oil to reach a depth of at least 2 inches (5cm), leaving a few inches to spare at the top. Heat oil to 340°F (171°C) over medium-high heat. When oil comes to temperature, brush any excess flour from the samosas 
  14.  Fry samosas, 5 at a time, turning them occasionally, until golden brown and puffed on all sides, 10 to 12 minutes (the oil temperature will drop significantly once the samosas are added; adjust heat to maintain temperature between 325-340°F/165-171°C). Avoid overcrowding the pot, as too many samosas will reduce the temperature of the oil and make the finished pastry soggy. Using a spider or slotted spoon, transfer cooked samosas to prepared baking sheet, and transfer to oven to keep warm.
  15. Skim any browned bits from oil and discard. Return oil to 340°F (171°C), and repeat with remaining samosas. Serve warm with chutney, such as mint or cilantro.

title: Traditional Victoria sponge with Raspberry & Vanilla Jam
content:
Enjoy a delightful afternoon tea with warm fruit scones, Victoria sponge with raspberry and vanilla jam, and the perfect scone topping of butter, jam, and cream.

 
recipe from Hawkshead Relish
 
 
Preparation time: 30 minutes
Cooking time: 45 minutes 
Serves: 8-10

 

Ingredients

For Victoria Sponge:

  • 4 eggs
  • 225g caster sugar
  • 225g self-raising flour
  • 225g softened butter
  • 2 teaspoons baking powder
  • ½ vanilla pod
  • 110g Hawkshead Relish Raspberry & Vanilla Jam
  • Icing sugar, for dusting

For The Scones:

  • 500g plain flour
  • 100g caster sugar
  • 125g softened butter
  • 65g mixed dried fruit
  • 2 large egg beaten
  • 250ml milk
  • 25g baking powder 

Method

For The Victoria Sponge:

Preheat the oven to 180°c.

  1. Break the eggs into a bowl and add the sugar, flour, baking powder, butter. Scrape out the vanilla seeds and add them to the bowl, then mix well using a hand mixer.
  2. Divide the batter equally between two greased and lined 20cm sandwich cake tins. Bake in the centre of the oven for 25 minutes or until golden and springy to the touch.
  3. Leave the sponges to cool in the tins for 5 minutes then carefully move to a wire rack. Once cooled completely, turn one cake over spread the underside with a thick layer of the Raspberry & Vanilla Jam. Top with the second cake and dust with icing sugar.

For The Scones:

Preheat the oven to 190°c.

  1. Sift the flour into a bowl, stir in the sugar then rub in the butter to breadcrumb consistency. Sprinkle in the dried fruit and pour in the beaten egg with three tablespoons of the milk. Bring together using a round-bladed knife to form a soft sticky dough, then place on a lightly floured worktop. Roll into a long tube like a swiss roll then cut into approximately 3 to 4cm rounds.
  2. Place the scones on a greased baking tray. Brush with a little milk, dust with a sprinkle of flour and place on the top shelf of the oven for 12 to 15 minutes until they are golden brown.

title: Umami-Glazed Salmon
content:
Perfectly baked bakkafrost salmon with the rich, savoury flavour of umami sauce, this recipe is an easy way to elevate your dinner game. A dish that’s both comforting and gourmet in every bite.

(serves 2–3)

Ingredients:

  • 2 Bakkafrost salmon fillets (about 150–180g each)

  • 3–4 tbsp umami Sauce (adjust to taste)

  • 1 tsp sesame oil (optional, for extra richness)

  • 1 clove garlic, minced (optional)

  • Sesame seeds and chopped spring onions, for garnish

Instructions:

  1. Preheat oven to 200°C (or 180°C fan). Line a baking tray with foil or parchment paper.

  2. Make the glaze in a small bowl, combine the umami Sauce, optional sesame oil, and garlic. Mix well.

  3. Coat the salmon:
    Place salmon fillets skin-side down on the tray. Spoon the glaze generously over the top of each fillet.

  4. Bake for 12–15 minutes, or until the salmon is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork. If you like a slightly caramelised top, broil/grill it for the last 1–2 minutes.

  5. Serve hot, garnished with sesame seeds and spring onions. Perfect with rice, noodles, or greens.

title: Rosemary & Garlic Lamb Rack
content:
Ingredients:

  • 4-6 cloves garlic, 
  • 6-8 pieces of Roaring Forties Lamb Rack
  • 6-8 Tablespoons of Extra Virgin Olive Oil
  • 20-40g of Butter
  • 6-8 sprigs of Rosemary 
  • 1 lime

    Optional Sides:

Maple Glazed Carrots
Radicchio Salad Mix & Cherry Tomatoes & a Pomegranate 
 
Steps:
Start by heating up the oil in a pan on medium to low heat. Add the sliced garlic cloves to the pan. Pour the garlic and oil in a bowl to cool. 

Strip off the Rosemary sprigs, place the other half of the oil in the pan to heat up. When the oil starts to turn green, place it in a bowl to cool. 

Zest the lime and set it aside.

On a separate baking tray, set the lamb cutlets flat down. Sprinkle a generous amount of salt and freshly ground black pepper on both sides. 

Add both rosemary oil and garlic oil to marinate. Massage the oils and herbs into the crevices of the meat. 

Let the lamb racks soak in the marinate for at least an hour refrigerated. 

Once ready, heat up the grill on medium to high heat. Put the butter on the grill, once the butter starts to sizzle, the grill is hot enough. As the butter is sizzling, use any remaining fresh herbs to season the butter. Place the lamb racks face down on the grill to cook. Once both sides of the lamb are no longer pink, they are ready to be served.

Sides:
(Radicchio salad) 
Chop cherry tomatoes and remove seeds from the pomegranate. Plate up and serve.

(Maple Glazed Carrots)
Trim off the baby carrots leaves to a short length, on a baking tray, drizzle olive oil, chilli flakes and maple syrup. Bake at 180 degrees for 10-15 mins and serve.

title: Salmon with Fennel, Blood Orange and Pistachio Salad
content:
Blackened Salmon with Fennel, Blood Orange and Pistachio Salad

by Karlie Verkerk

 

Serves 4-6

Cook time 30 minutes

 

INGREDIENTS

1.4 kg side of salmon

2 tbsp onion powder

2 tbsp sweet paprika

1½ tbsp brown sugar

2 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)

2 tsp fine sea salt

1 tbsp white balsamic vinegar

3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil

2 small blood oranges

1 small fennel

Handful of basil leaves
¼ cup pistachios, roughly chopped



METHOD

  1. Preheat the oven to 180°C. Place the side of salmon skin-side down on a large baking tray lined with baking paper.

  2. In a small bowl, combine the onion powder, sweet paprika, brown sugar and salt. Sprinkle evenly over the salmon and use the back of a spoon to spread out so the salmon is covered completely. Place in the oven and bake for 16-20 minutes, or until the salmon is just cooked through at the thickest end. Note: the salmon will continue cooking slightly once it’s removed from the oven.

  3. Meanwhile, combine vinegar and olive oil in a small jar with a pinch of salt; top with a lid and shake to combine. 

  4. Peel oranges then remove segments with a sharp knife. Thinly shave the fennel with a mandolin (reserve fennel fronds). Place in a large mixing bowl with fennel fronds, basil and pistachios. When ready to serve, drizzle salad with dressing and toss gently to combine.

  5. Serve salmon on a large plate, topped with orange and fennel salad.

title: Rainbow Gummies
content:
These Rainbow Dino Gummies are a breeze to make – done in 40 mins and serves 18. Bursting with fruity Gutsy Gummies flavours such as blueberry, strawberry, and mango.

Ingredients

3 × 200 ml boiling water (separated)

2 × 100 ml boiling water (separated)

2x moulds of your choice

⅓ cup Gutsy Gummies Blueberry

⅓ cup Gutsy Gummies Strawberry

⅓ cup Gutsy Gummies Mango

Method

  1. Mix 100ml of room temperature water with each flavour of gummy, then add 200ml of recently boiled water to each
  2. Pour into Dino moulds on an angle (we used a chopping board and a glass to prop up the moulds). Only fill half the mould. Refrigerate for 10-15mins or until set

title: Linguine with White Wine Sauce
content:
A quick, elegant dish perfect with shrimp, scallops, or grilled chicken

Ingredients:

250g dried linguine

2 tablespoons olive oil

3–4 garlic cloves, minced

1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional, for a little heat)

1/2 teaspoon salt (adjust to taste)

1/4 teaspoon black pepper

1/2 cup dry white wine

2 tablespoons unsalted butter

Fresh lemon juice (optional, for finishing)

Reserved pasta water (up to 1/2 cup)

Instructions:

  1. Cook Linguine
    Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the linguine according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve up to 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain the rest.

  2. Sauté Aromatics
    In a large saucepan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté for about 1 minute, or until fragrant and lightly golden.

  3. Make the Sauce
    Add salt, pepper, white wine, and butter to the pan. Stir and let it simmer for 2–3 minutes until slightly reduced.

  4. Toss with Pasta
    Add the drained linguine directly into the sauce. Toss to coat. If the sauce is too thick, add a splash of the reserved pasta water until it reaches your desired consistency.

  5. Finish and Serve
    Add a squeeze of lemon juice, if using, for brightness. Serve immediately with shrimp, scallops, grilled chicken, or enjoy on its own! Lastly, top with freshly chopped parsley or grated Parmesan (if not serving with seafood) for extra flavour. (optional)

content:
Fruit Jelly Moulds with Gutsy Gummies

A colourful treat for the whole family with instant nutrition and fruity refreshment - these Fruit Jelly Moulds are ultra easy to prepare and even easier to devour! The best part about these wiggly wonders is the vitamin C, protein and gut loving goodness they bring, all thanks to Gutsy Gummies (now available in Little Farms!)

Pantry Items

  • 2 x 1/3 cup of Gutsy Gummies (two flavours, or ⅔ one flavour)

  • 3 cups chopped fruit (strawberries, rockmelon, blueberries, grapes - fruit of choice!)

Method

  • Refrigerate for 30 minutes, or until set.

  • Turn out the gummies onto a plate or store them in an airtight container. Enjoy!

title: Udon with Tofu and Vegetables
content:
A wholesome, flavour-packed dish for fans of bold, oriental-inspired meals.

Made with Double Concentrated Tomato Paste
For rich, intense tomato flavour, Mutti’s Tomato Paste is the perfect choice—enhancing both depth and texture in every dish.

Ready in 30 min (Prep: 15 min / Cook: 15 min)
Serves 4 | Easy | Vegan & Vegetarian

Ingredients

Main

  • 400 g fresh udon

  • 350 g silken tofu

  • 1 tsp turmeric

  • 100 g onion (sliced)

  • 100 g carrot (julienned)

  • 100 g zucchini (julienned)

  • Sesame oil (as needed)

  • Kala namak / black salt  (to taste)

  • Toasted sesame seeds (for garnish)

Sauce

  • 60 ml soy sauce

  • 1 tbsp Mutti Double Concentrated Tomato Paste

  • 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds

  • 1 garlic clove (crushed)

Method

  1. Prepare the sauce. In a small bowl, combine the soy sauce, Double Concentrated Tomato Paste, crushed garlic, and toasted sesame seeds. Mix well and set aside.
  2. Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan, then add the silken tofu and break it apart with the tip of a spatula.
  3. Add the turmeric and mix well.
  4. Let the tofu cook over high heat until it has released all its water. Once ready, season it with kala namak salt and set aside.
  5. In the same pan used for the tofu, heat a drizzle of oil, then add the sliced onion and sauté over high heat for a couple of minutes.
  6. Add the julienned carrots and zucchini and continue cooking over high heat for five minutes, stirring constantly.
  7. Meanwhile, bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook the udon for a couple of minutes.
  8. Once ready, drain the udon and add them to the pan with the vegetables over high heat. Then, add the sauce and the silken tofu.
  9. Stir-fry the udon in the pan for a couple of minutes.
  10. Garnish the udon with a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds.

title: Cauliflower Pizza
content:
Try this quick, gluten-free, low-carb vegetarian pizza—tasty, versatile, and topped with the best, like Mutti Polpa.

Made with Mutti Polpa
Freshly picked flavour in every spoon—Mutti Polpa blends finely chopped tomatoes with their own juice for rich, vibrant taste.

Ready in 50 min (Prep: 10 min / Cook: 40 min)
Serves 2 | Vegetarian | Medium difficulty

Ingredients

Base

  • 1 kg cauliflower

  • 1 egg

  • 20 g peanut oil

  • 1 garlic clove, crushed

  • 1 tsp oregano

  • 1 tbsp grated cheese

  • 50 g finely chopped mozzarella

  • Salt & pepper

Topping

  • 200 g Mutti Polpa Rustica Di Pomodoro

  • 150 g finely chopped mozzarella

  • 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil

  • ½ tsp oregano

  • Salt & pepper

  • Fresh basil

Method

  1. Prepare Cauliflower: Wash and separate florets, then pulse in a food processor until rice-like.

  2. Cook Base: Sauté in a non-stick pan with oil and salt for 10 mins.

  3. Make Dough: Mix cooked cauliflower with egg, cheese, garlic, oregano, mozzarella, pepper, and a pinch of salt.

  4. Bake Crust: Spread mixture onto a lined 28cm tray. Bake at 180°C (fan) for 30 mins until golden. Flip and bake briefly if needed.

  5. Add Toppings: Mix Mutti Polpa with oregano, oil, salt, and pepper. Spread over crust, top with mozzarella, and bake for 8–10 mins.

  6. Serve: Finish with extra oregano and fresh basil.

title: Viral High Protein Beef Bowl
content:
With over 15g of protein, this bowl is a flavour powerhouse! Ground beef simmered in Beef Bone Broth, creamy cottage cheese, avocado, caramelised sweet potato, and fresh spinach, all topped with a spicy-sweet honey drizzle. Easy, satisfying, and ready in 35 minutes!

Recipe from Nutra Organics

Ingredients

1 large sweet potato, diced

2 tbsp olive oil

Pinch of salt & pepper

1/2 tsp cinnamon

800g ground beef

2 tbsp Beef Bone Broth Concentrate Native Herbs

1 tsp garlic powder

1 tsp onion powder

1 tbsp smoked paprika

1 cup cottage cheese

2 avocados, halved and sliced

2 cups baby spinach

2 tbsp honey

2 tsp chili flakes

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.

  2. Toss sweet potato with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, pepper, and cinnamon. Bake for 25-30 mins until soft and caramelised.

  3. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a pan over high heat. Add ground beef and cook until browned.

  4. Lower heat and add Beef Bone Broth Concentrate, garlic powder, onion powder, and smoked paprika. Cook for another couple of minutes.

  5. Assemble the bowl by layering sweet potato, beef, cottage cheese, avocado, and spinach. Drizzle with honey and sprinkle chili flakes.

Enjoy your protein-packed, flavourful bowl in just 35 minutes!

title: Berry Macadamia Parfait with Low Sugar Granola
featured_image_title: Berry Macadamia Parfait with Low Sugar Granola
content:
TIME

30 minutes

SERVES

4

CREATED BY

Sarah DeNardi/ Brookfarm

SUMMARY

A rich in berries, low in sugar crunchy macadamia parfait that is as beautiful as it is delicious. Layered with zesty homemade berry compote, creamy Greek yogurt, and Brookfarm’s crunchy gourmet Low Sugar Macadamia Granola – an easy to make cafe style parfait at home.

 

Ingredients

Berry Compote

  • 4 cups mixed berries (fresh or frozen)
  • 2 tbsp monk fruit sweetener (or your preferred sweetener) 
  • Juice and zest of 1 lemon (divided)
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1 cinnamon stick (optional)
  • 1–2 lemon myrtle leaves (optional)
  • 3 tsp arrowroot or cornflour
  • ¼ tsp ground ginger or 1 tsp freshly grated ginger (optional)

 

Parfait Layers

  • 1 cup fresh berries
  • 2 cups thick Greek yogurt
  • 120g Brookfarm Low Sugar Granola Macadamia & Raspberry

 

Method

  • In a saucepan, combine berries, monk fruit sweetener, lemon zest, vanilla, and cinnamon stick/lemon myrtle (if using). Stir in 1 tbsp of lemon juice. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
  • In a small bowl, mix arrowroot with the remaining lemon juice. Stir into the berry mix along with ginger (if using) and cook for 2–3 more minutes until slightly thickened.
  • Remove from heat, discard cinnamon stick and lemon myrtle leaves. Cool completely.
  • How to Assemble: A spoonful of fresh berries | ¼ of the berry compote | A generous layer of Greek yogurt | A sprinkle of Brookfarm granola on top

 

Recipe Notes & Tips

  • Make ahead: Assemble parfaits up to a day ahead – just leave granola off until serving.
  • Storage: Compote keeps in the fridge for 1 week or freeze up to 3 months.
  • Sweetener info: Monk fruit sweetener is naturally derived and zero-calorie. Look for one with a 1:1 sugar replacement ratio.
