title: Fresh Peach Waffles
content:
Celebrate stone fruit season with this fresh peach upgrade to your classic waffle mix. Juicy chunks of ripe peach add a naturally sweet, fruity burst to every bite—perfect for a sunny brunch or a summery dessert.

Made using Kialla Pure Foods Organic Waffle Mix - Classic

Ingredients:

Kialla Pure Foods Organic Waffle Mix - Classic
190ml milk (or to the line on the bottle)
1 fresh ripe peach, peeled and finely chopped
Optional: ½ tsp cinnamon or vanilla extract
Butter or oil (for greasing the waffle maker)
Maple syrup, yoghurt, or more peach slices to serve

Method:

  1. Preheat your waffle maker to a medium setting.

  2. Shake the bottle to loosen the dry mix.

  3. Remove the lid (don’t discard it).

  4. Fill the bottle with 190ml of milk (or to the marked line). You can use any milk you prefer.

  5. Optional: Add a pinch of cinnamon or a splash of vanilla extract to the bottle.

  6. Replace the lid, turn the bottle upside down, and tap gently to loosen the mix. Shake the bottle well for 1 minute. Let it sit for 2 minutes to thicken.

  7. Chop the fresh peach and fold the pieces directly into the batter only just before cooking, or spoon some into each waffle section of the waffle maker before pouring the batter.

  8. Grease the waffle maker, pour in the peachy batter, and cook for 3–4 minutes or until golden.

  9. Serve warm with more fresh peaches, maple syrup, or a dollop of yoghurt.

Storage Tip:

  1. If you plan to store any leftover batter, don’t add peaches to the bottle.
  2. Store batter in the fridge for up to 5 days, then add chopped fresh peaches when you’re ready to cook.

1 1/2 cups fruit, fresh or frozen

1 cup/ 240g plain greek yogurt

275g dark chocolate or carob chocolate 

3 tablespoons pistachio butter

Sprinkle of salt flakes

 

Method

  1. Cut fruit into chunks

  2. Combine yogurt and fruit

  3. Drop approximately 2 tablespoon-sized clusters onto baking parchment

  4. Set in the freezer for around 2-3 hours

  5. Chop the chocolate, then melt in a double boiler or in 30-second intervals in the microwave, mixing in between intervals to prevent burning

  6. Dunk clusters into chocolate, then drizzle with pistachio butter

  7. Sprinkle with salt flakes

  8. Return to freezer for another hour to firm up (or inhale immediately)

title: Brownies and Pancakes Tea-Time Snack
content:
Double Chocolate Brownies

Ingredients:

  • 1 jar brownie mix (contains plain flour, baking powder, cocoa powder, brown sugar, dark chocolate chips, and white chocolate chips)

  • 150g cooled, melted butter

  • 3 eggs, beaten

Instructions:

  1. Preheat your oven to 180°C (fan or conventional).

  2. Line a 20cm x 20cm square baking tin with parchment paper.

  3. In a large bowl, combine the contents of the jar with the melted butter and beaten eggs.

  4. Mix well until fully combined.

  5. Pour the mixture into the prepared tin and spread evenly.

  6. Bake for 25–35 minutes, or until the top is set and a skewer inserted into the centre comes out with just a few moist crumbs.

  7. Allow to cool before slicing into squares.

Enjoy your rich, double chocolate brownies!

 

Classic Pancakes Using Kialla Organic Pancake Mix

Ingredients:

  • 1 cup Kialla Organic Pancake Mix

  • ¾ cup milk (adjust for thinner or thicker pancakes)

  • 1 egg

  • 1 tbsp melted butter or neutral oil (plus extra for cooking)

 

Instructions:

  1. Mix the Batter
    In a bowl, whisk together the Kialla Organic Pancake Mix, milk, egg, and melted butter until smooth. Avoid overmixing.

  2. Rest (Optional)
    Let the batter rest for 5 minutes for fluffier pancakes.

  3. Heat the Pan
    Heat a non-stick pan or lightly greased skillet over medium heat.

  4. Cook the Pancakes
    Pour about ¼ cup of batter onto the pan for each pancake.
    Cook for 1–2 minutes or until bubbles appear on the surface and the edges begin to set.

  5. Flip and Finish
    Flip and cook for another 1–2 minutes until golden and cooked through.

  6. Serve Warm
    Stack them together and enjoy with fresh fruits (strawberries) and organic honey from Little Farms!

Note: For a dairy-free version, use plant-based milk and oil instead of butter.

title: Dragonfruit and Mango Smoothie Cup
content:
Dragonfruit & Mango Smoothie Cup

 

Ingredients

1 cup frozen dragon fruit chunks

1 cup frozen mango chunks

1/2 cup frozen banana slices

3/4 cup COYO Vanilla Coconut Yoghurt

1/2 cup plant milk (almond, oat, or coconut milk)

1–2 tsp maple syrup or honey (optional, for added sweetness)

1/4 cup granola (for topping)

1/4 cup hemp seeds

 

Method

  1. Blend the Mango First: Start by placing the frozen mango, frozen banana, COYO Vanilla Coconut Yoghurt, hemp seeds and plant milk into a high-speed blender. Blend on low, using a tamper to push the mixture down and around until smooth and creamy. The mixture should be thick and spoonable. If it’s too thick, add a splash of plant milk until the desired consistency is reached. Taste and add maple syrup or honey if extra sweetness is needed.
  2. Prepare the Glasses: Use the back of a spoon to dollop and spread a teaspoon of COYO Vanilla Coconut Yoghurt around the inside of the glass to create a fun, swirly “ice cream” effect.
  3. Create the Layers: Pour half of the mango mixture into the prepared glasses or bowls, leaving the remaining half in the blender.
  4. Add the Dragon Fruit Layer: To the blender, add the frozen dragon fruit and blend until smooth. Pour the vibrant pink dragon fruit mixture on top of the mango layer in the glasses, creating a stunning layered effect.
  5. Top and Serve: Sprinkle granola on top for crunch and extra flavor. Serve immediately and enjoy this deliciously tropical layered smoothie!

  • 3 tbsp Vegetable oil
  • Pistachio Papi

 

Method

  • The kefir must be warm or at room temperature.

  • Add sifted flour and mix until there are no lumps.
  • Pour in the boiling water and mix everything quickly.
  • Add vegetable oil and mix well.
  • You can start frying the pancakes immediately.
  • Preheat the pan well before adding the batter.
  • Once the pancakes are cooked, brush them with melted butter and Pistachio Papi.

title: Sunny Chard Skillet with Avocado
content:
Sunny chard skillet with avocado perfect for a vibrant, nourishing breakfast or brunch dish!
Recipe by Sharon: @patchmasterchef 

 

Ingredients


•⁠ Avocado 
•⁠ Eggs
• ⁠Swiss Chard
•⁠ Garlic
•⁠ Onion
•⁠ Olive oil
•⁠ Coriander and cucumbers (optional)

 

Method

 

•⁠  ⁠Chop the garlic, onions into small cubes.

•⁠  ⁠Crack 3 eggs. (Tip: have them in separate bowls if you want the eggs to be evenly distributed)

•⁠  ⁠Continue to cook the eggs till the doneness you like. 
•⁠  ⁠Place the sliced avocado in between the eggs. 
•⁠  ⁠Sprinkle some paprika and sea salt flakes on the avocado and the eggs.

title: Sesame Oil Chicken
content:
A comforting dish passed down through generations; straight from Grandma’s kitchen!
This simple yet flavourful recipe brings together the best of ginger, sesame oil, and chicken.

Recipe by @tfeatkitchen

 

Ingredients: 

- 450g mid joint chicken wings
- 30ml sesame oil (divided into 3 parts: 10ml each)
- 10g old ginger, thinly sliced
- 2 star anise
- 70g fresh black fungus
- 8 mushrooms, halved
- 3g corn starch + 10ml water (for slurry)
- Pinch of salt (optional)
- Sesame seeds, for garnish
- 2 stalks spring onions, chopped, for garnish

Chicken Marinade:

- 6ml light soy sauce
- 6ml dark soy sauce
- 6ml oyster sauce
- 10ml sesame oil

Sauce mixture (for main dish):

- 200ml water
- 6ml light soy sauce
- 6ml dark soy sauce
- 6ml oyster sauce

 

Instructions:

Marinate the Chicken:
Mix chicken wings with chicken marinade. Let it marinate for at least 4 hours in the fridge.

Main dish:
1. In a pot, heat 10ml sesame oil. Fry ginger slices and star anise until fragrant and slightly browned.
2. Add marinated chicken wings to the pot. Fry both sides for around 2 minutes, or until slightly charred.
3. Pour in the sauce mixture and bring to a boil. Lower heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
4. Add black fungus and mushrooms, then continue simmering for another 15 minutes.
5. Stir in corn starch mixture and bring to a quick boil to thicken the sauce.
6. Add a pinch of salt (if desired), garnish with spring onions, sesame seeds, and a final drizzle of sesame oil.

Pair with barley rice and steamed broccolini for a nourishing, well-balanced meal!

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

❤️ What makes this dish delicious? Sesame oil. Ginger. Chicken. That’s the magic trio!

title: Beef Stir Fry
content:
Ingredients: 

Beef Stir Fry
- 1 pack of LF Sliced Beef
- 1.5 tsp Black Pepper
- 2 tbsp Oyster Sauce 
- 1 tbsp Umami Sauce
- 1 tsp of Baking Soda
- 3 tbsp of Cornstarch  
- 2 tbsp of Oil 

Sauce
- 2 tbsp of Umami Sauce
- 1.5 tbsp of Minced Garlic 
- 0.5-1 tbsp of Black Pepper 
- 1.5 tbsp of Worcestershire sauce

Beef Stock
- 1/2 head of Broccoli 
- 1-2 Bell Peppers
- 1 pack of Little Farms Organic Shiitake Mushrooms
- 1/4 Cup of Minced Garlic 
- 1/2 Carrot

 

Instructions:

1. Prepare your desired portion of steamed Jasmine rice. 

2. Ground or pound 1/4 cup of black peppercorns.

3. Start marinating the beef with 1/2 of the crushed black pepper, oyster sauce, soy sauce, baking soda, cornstarch, and egg white. Massage well and set aside.

4. Start on the sauce by mixing the Umami sauce, minced garlic, black pepper and Worcestershire sauce.

5. In a pan, add 1 tbsp of olive oil and turn the heat up to medium-high. 

6. Once the pan is hot, add the beef and let it sit for 30 seconds before adding the sliced mushrooms for 3-4 minutes. 

7. Remove and set aside. 

8. In the same pan, add in sliced red onion and sauce for 1-2 minutes. Next add in the peppers and sauté for 1-2 minutes. 

9. Finally, add in the broccoli and beef stock. When the stir-fry is well-combined, serve with a generous portion of Jasmine rice and enjoy!

title: A New Way to Eat Well in the CBD: Little Farms Opens at Raffles Place
content:
• Launch of Little Farms’ eighth retail outlet in Singapore

  • Located at street level within One Raffles Place, offering grab-and-go café menu and retail store

  • All-natural, ethically sourced products including fresh produce, ethically sourced meats, wines, clean-label snacks and all-natural ready meals

  • Takeaway-only menu at Little Farms Café features nutritious breakfasts, protein-rich lunches, salads, wraps and smoothies

 

< Outside Little Farms Raffles Place >

 

SINGAPORE, 16 JULY 2025 — We have opened our doors at Little Farms Raffles Place, bringing our trusted promise of quality, clean, and ethically sourced food to Singapore’s Central Business District. Located at street level within One Raffles Place, the newly designed 2,600 square foot space combines a specialty grocer with a takeaway-focused food counter tailored to the CBD crowd. At its heart is a menu of nourishing, ready-to-go dishes and drinks, all made fresh daily using the same high-quality ingredients found on Little Farms’ shelves.

As with every Little Farms outlet, customers can trust that every item has been rigorously screened for quality. Each product is sourced through a trusted network of ethical suppliers and assessed against Little Farms’ banned ingredient list, which excludes over 200 harmful chemicals, artificial additives and preservatives. A dedicated buying team is on the ground throughout the year, working directly with farms across the globe to source produce at peak ripeness. Thanks to cold chain logistics, fruits and vegetables are delivered from farm to shelf within 48 hours of harvest, allowing them to ripen naturally and retain their full nutritional value. From ready meals to raw ingredients, every item reflects our commitment to all-natural ingredients, ethical sourcing and full transparency.

Joe Stevens, CEO of Little Farms, shares, “Having worked in the CBD for many years, I know first-hand how hard it can be to find convenient, nutritious food and great coffee in one place. With our new location at One Raffles Place, we’re bringing that solution to the heart of the city. Everything we do is shaped by the needs of the community, and we hope this new store adds a little ease and enjoyment to the workday.”

As Little Farms’ first outlet in Singapore’s Central Business District, the interior was conceptualised as a greenhouse farm by AArticle, the experiential design arm of Architology Interiors. Taking inspiration from the iconic Raffles Place lawn directly fronting the store, the space was envisioned as a lush, blooming communal garden set against the backdrop of concrete, steel and glass skyscrapers. The design promotes a sense of fresh harvests and encourages a mindful approach to healthy living within an urban environment.

 

< The design promotes a sense of fresh harvests >

 

Little Farms Café: Made for the City

Little Farms Café at Raffles Place is designed for the fast-paced CBD lifestyle, offering a broad menu of fresh, satisfying meals made with premium, all-natural ingredients. The ready-to-go menu caters perfectly to those looking for nourishing breakfasts, protein-rich lunches or wholesome mid-afternoon bites. The café combines quality and convenience, with every item prepared fresh daily using ingredients shoppers can also find on Little Farms’ shelves.

Breakfast features the likes of the LF Breakfast Slider with avocado, free-range scrambled eggs, cheddar and sriracha mayo, the Organic Açai Bowl with granola, banana, strawberry, mango and coconut as well as Pistachio Toast layered with house-made pistachio butter and roasted kernels. 

The lunch menu showcases filled ciabattas, focaccias, wraps and salads, all made fresh daily. Highlights include the Miso Mushroom Melt with baby spinach, Emmental and sun-dried tomato; the Chicken Caesar Salad with poached chicken breast, bacon bits and anchovy aioli. The Pulled Lamb Wrap, made with slow-cooked lamb leg, red cabbage and pickled onion, brings bold flavour, while lighter dishes include the Japanese Soba Salad with edamame and wakame, and the Quinoa Romaine Bowl with baby spinach, pomegranate and walnuts. 

The beverage menu includes a new line-up of high-protein smoothies, such as Red Berry Dynamo, Big Matcha Energy and Chocolate Flex, alongside barista-made coffee, teas and cold drinks.

To round things off, a daily selection of viennoiserie and fresh bakes from Starter Lab is available, including croissants, morning buns, scones and muffins, alongside indulgent pastries such as tiramisu, NY cheesecake and flourless praline cake.

Whether dining in or grabbing something to go, Little Farms Café offers the kind of food that leaves you feeling good — made with care, using the same high-quality ingredients found on its shelves.

 

 

 

The Retail Experience

The market at Little Farms Raffles Place brings together the full breadth of the brand’s trusted offering, from the freshest seasonal fruits and vegetables to ethically sourced meats, essential pantry staples, clean-label snacks, fine wines, craft beers and dairy. With a wide range of products catering to specific dietary needs — including vegan, keto and gluten-free options — the store is designed to support a healthier way of living across every lifestyle and preference.

Every cut of meat at Little Farms is sourced from trusted farms with a focus on sustainability, traceability and animal welfare. This includes Green Meadows Beef, a family-owned farm in Taranaki, New Zealand, producing premium grass-fed Angus beef with full control over both farming and manufacturing as well as Bostock Brothers Fresh Organic Chicken from New Zealand, known for its clean, antibiotic-free farming and exceptional flavour.

Over 75 percent of the wine range is sourced directly from vineyards, offering customers access to exclusive labels and cellar door pricing. These sit alongside a rotating selection of craft beers, providing options to suit every palate and occasion. Ready meals and prepared foods meet the same uncompromising standards as the rest of the store — made only with natural ingredients, free from artificial additives or preservatives.

 

Fresh Bakes from Starter Lab

Freshly baked each morning, the selection at Little Farms Raffles Place includes a rotating range of artisanal breads and pastries from Starter Lab, the brand’s in-house bakery. Known for its commitment to time-honoured techniques and premium ingredients, Starter Lab brings a handcrafted touch to everyday essentials.

Bestsellers include classic sourdough loaves, flaky croissants, pain au chocolat, focaccia and baguettes — all made without additives or preservatives. Perfect for a quick breakfast, a working lunch or to elevate your home pantry, these bakes reflect the same commitment to quality and clean ingredients found across the rest of the store.

title: Fried Chicken Waffle Lemak
content:
Inspired by Nasi Lemak, Fried Chicken Waffle Lemak is a dish that uses coconut milk like how it is used to cook the rice in Nasi Lemak. Coconut fried chicken fried with flour mixed with desiccated coconut. Imagine waffles infused with a hint of coconut milk and topped with fried chicken. It is served with a dollop of spicy sambal, crushed crunchy peanuts, cucumbers, an omelette, a side of caramelized onions and chili coconut mayonnaise. All ingredients from Little Farms.

Recipe by @patchmasterchef.

Ingredients 

Coconut waffles (3 x 8inch round waffles)
- 200g all-purpose flour
- 50g coconut flour
- 2 tbsp coconut sugar
- 2 tsp baking powder 
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 2 eggs
- 55ml coconut oil
- 370ml coconut milk
- 50g desiccated coconut

Coconut fried chicken
- 2 pieces of chicken thighs
- 250ml coconut milk
- 150g all-purpose flour
- 50g desiccated coconut
- 1/2 tsp + a pinch of salt
- Oil for frying 

Caramelised onions
- 2 red onions
- Coconut sugar

Sides
- Omelette
- 2 eggs
- Cucumber 
- A handful of crushed peanuts

 

Instructions

Caramelised Onions
1.⁠ ⁠Thinly slice the onions.
2.⁠ ⁠In a pan over medium-low heat, sauté the onions in olive oil until soft and translucent.
3.⁠ ⁠Add coconut sugar and continue to cook slowly until the onions are deeply caramelised.

 

Coconut Waffles
1.⁠ ⁠In a large bowl, whisk together the dry ingredients, flour, sugar, baking powder, desiccated coconut and salt.
2.⁠ ⁠In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs, coconut oil, and coconut milk until well combined.
3.⁠ ⁠Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients. Stir until just combined — the batter will be slightly grainy due to the desiccated coconut.
4.⁠ ⁠Preheat and grease your waffle iron.
5.⁠ ⁠Ladle in the batter and cook according to your waffle maker's instructions until golden and crisp.

 

Coconut Fried Chicken (Marinate at least 1 hour in advance)
1.⁠ ⁠Place chicken thighs in a bowl and cover with coconut milk. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
2.⁠ ⁠In a shallow tray, mix flour, salt, and desiccated coconut.
3.⁠ ⁠Remove the chicken from the marinade and coat each piece thoroughly in the flour mixture, ensuring all sides are well covered.
4.⁠ ⁠Heat oil in a deep pan to 180°C . Fry the chicken for 12–15 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through.
5.⁠ ⁠Drain and season with a pinch of salt.

 

Sides
1. Make a simple 2-egg omelette.
2. Slice fresh cucumber.
3. Lightly crush peanuts.

 

To Assemble
Place fried chicken, omelette and cucumber on a warm coconut waffle. Sprinkle with crushed peanuts and a little extra desiccated coconut for texture. Add a generous dollop of Everiday Sambal and served with a spoonful of chilli coconut mayonnaise and caramelised onions by the side.
